meanings.meaning: To be destroyed or wiped out. God promises that never again will all living things be destroyed by a flood of water covering the whole earth.

idioms.idiom: a wild donkey of a man

meanings.meaning: Ishmael would be wild and hard to tame, like a wild donkey. He would fight with others and they with him, but he would remain independent.
To walk before God means to live and obey Him, knowing His eye is always on you. In Genesis, God tells Abram to be firmly set on obeying Him.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean a person lost his place among God's people and their blessings, or that God would end his life early.

idioms.idiom: possess the gates of their enemies

meanings.meaning: Abraham's descendants, his children and all the later generations, will defeat their enemies and rule over them. A city's gate held its defenses and its judges, so it stood for the whole city's strength.
Jacob means his sons made him hated by the people around them. Now those neighbors might join together against his family and destroy them.

idioms.idiom: I will go down to Sheol mourning for my son

meanings.meaning: Jacob says he will keep grieving until he dies and goes to the place of the dead, where he expects to meet his son Joseph. He refuses to be comforted.
Reuben means they must answer for what they did to Joseph. The notes say their guilty consciences were bothering them, and they felt God's justice was catching up with them.

idioms.idiom: you will bring my gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow

meanings.meaning: Jacob says that if Benjamin dies on the trip, his sons will cause him to die an old man full of sadness. The grief would be too heavy for him to bear.

idioms.idiom: Joseph's own hands will close your eyes

meanings.meaning: God promises that Joseph will be with Jacob when he dies and will close his eyes. This was an old custom, done for the dead by the closest relative or friend.

idioms.idiom: you went up to your father's bed

meanings.meaning: Reuben sinned sexually against his father Jacob, treating Jacob's marriage bed with lust and disrespect. Because of this, he lost the firstborn's place of honor and leadership.

idioms.idiom: nor the staff from between his feet

meanings.meaning: A lawgiver sat between a king's feet, so this line means Judah's rule would keep going without ceasing until the Messiah comes. After that, Judah would have no king or judge of its own.

idioms.idiom: The scepter will not depart from Judah

meanings.meaning: A scepter is a ruler's staff, a sign of power. Bible teachers differ: it may mean Judah's rulers keep their authority, or that Judah stays a tribe, until the promised King sent by God comes.
Issachar is compared to a strong donkey that lies down with its loads. His tribe would work hard at farming and choose peaceful rest, even paying taxes, instead of fighting to be free.

idioms.idiom: Naphtali is a doe set free

meanings.meaning: Naphtali is pictured as a deer set free. Bible teachers aren't sure if it means a tribe living freely in good land or one that wins with gentle words.
Machir's children were born while Joseph was alive, and he helped raise them. Teachers say he taught them as family head, or held them on his lap like a loving grandfather.
God's power acting to punish. Here His hand strikes Egypt's animals with a terrible sickness, and it is stronger than Pharaoh's hold on the Israelites.
Bible teachers aren't sure what this meant. It may mean the person was shut out from God's people and lost his place among them, or it may mean he was put to death.

idioms.idiom: a hand was lifted up toward the throne of the LORD

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean God swore a serious promise, or that Amalek raised a hand against God's people; some think "throne" was a copying mistake for "banner."

idioms.idiom: Do not draw near to a woman

meanings.meaning: God told the people to stay away from sexual relations, even with their own wives, for a short time. It was part of getting ready for the third day, when God would speak to them.

idioms.idiom: the LORD will break out against them

meanings.meaning: God would suddenly punish them. The notes show this warning was meant to fill the people with awe, so even the priests must get ready and treat God as holy before coming near Him.

idioms.idiom: He will break out against them

meanings.meaning: If the priests or people push past the boundary to get up to the LORD, He will punish them, and many could die. The warning was meant to keep them safe.

idioms.idiom: visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children

meanings.meaning: God brings judgment on sin, especially idol worship, so its results reach children and grandchildren. Bible teachers differ: Clarke says only children who copy their parents are judged; others say children bear their parents' guilt.

idioms.idiom: take the name of the LORD your God in vain

meanings.meaning: To use God's name in an empty or untrue way. Bible teachers agree this forbids false oaths in His name, and many say it also forbids careless, disrespectful talk about Him.
"Within your gates" means in the cities, towns, and villages of your land, not just inside your own house. So the foreigner within your gates is a foreign worker who has settled among the Israelites.

idioms.idiom: eye for eye, tooth for tooth

meanings.meaning: The punishment must match the harm done, and judges decided it, not people seeking revenge. Bible teachers aren't sure if it meant literal injury or a matching payment.

idioms.idiom: I will fulfill the number of your days

meanings.meaning: God promises that His people will live out all the days meant for them and not die too young. Bible teachers say this means reaching a good old age, as a blessing.
Aaron, the high priest, took on the blame for the sins and mistakes in the people's holy gifts. The gold plate on his forehead made up for these, so God would accept the gifts.

idioms.idiom: cut off from among his people

meanings.meaning: A man who killed an ox, lamb, or goat without bringing it to God's tent was treated like a murderer. He was removed from his people, perhaps by death from the leaders or from God.
Stubborn and hard to lead. Like an ox that won't let a yoke be put on its neck, the people would not bow to God's commands.
It means worshiping other gods instead of the true God. Gill says foreign wives, raised from childhood to worship their gods, would long for them and could tempt Israel's sons into idol worship too.

idioms.idiom: the salt of the covenant of your God

meanings.meaning: Salt added to every offering. Salt keeps food from spoiling, so it stood for a lasting promise between God and His people, and for pure, faithful worship.

idioms.idiom: a man lies with a woman

meanings.meaning: This means a man and woman have sexual relations, not just sleep in the same bed. Afterward both had to wash and were "unclean" until evening.
It means a man and woman have sex, not just lie near each other. If this happens during her period, he becomes ceremonially unclean for seven days.

idioms.idiom: cut him off from among his people

meanings.meaning: God would turn against anyone who ate blood and remove that person from His people. If the sin was known, the person was sentenced to death; if it was secret, God Himself would punish him.

idioms.idiom: I will set My face against that person

meanings.meaning: God's "face" shows His anger. He turns against a person who eats blood, and that person would be cut off, no longer a part of God's people.
He is still guilty and will be punished. If someone skips the washing, the sin stays on him, and he must face the penalty for it.

idioms.idiom: cut him off from his people

meanings.meaning: God would remove the guilty person from among his people, ending his life. Bible teachers say God might do this Himself if the people did not punish the crime or it could not be proved.
To look the other way on purpose. The people ignore the crime and don't report or punish it, maybe because they don't care or because they secretly approve of it.
It means worshiping the false god Molech. God had joined Israel to Himself like a husband to a wife, so serving another god was like being unfaithful in marriage.

idioms.idiom: cut off from among their people

meanings.meaning: Both people would be "cut off from among their people" as punishment. The notes show the crime was treated as very serious, but they don't explain exactly what being cut off means.
To be held responsible for a sin and face its punishment. Here, priests who ate God's holy things while unclean, or who ignored His sanctuary, would be punished and die.
To "humble himself" means to "afflict your souls" on the Day of Atonement, when the whole year's sins were wiped away. Anyone who refused faced the harshest punishment.

idioms.idiom: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth

meanings.meaning: The punishment should match the harm done, with the same injury given back. One Bible teacher says it meant paying a fair price instead of being hurt the same way.
An "uncircumcised heart" is a proud, foolish, sinful heart that has not turned to God. The verse says that if their hearts were humbled, they would admit their troubles were God's punishment.
A wife turns away from her husband and is unfaithful to him with another man. The notes say this law handled cases where the husband strongly suspected her but had no witnesses.
To "go astray" here means a wife turned away from her husband and was unfaithful to him. The notes say it means she had sex with a man who is not her husband.
She will suffer the punishment for her own wrongdoing. The notes say that if she was guilty, the bitter water would hurt her, and her husband would not be blamed for it.

idioms.idiom: cause His face to shine upon you

meanings.meaning: A prayer that God would be kind to His people and let them feel His loving presence, like seeing His happy, peaceful face. Bible teachers say it also brings light and knowing Him better.

idioms.idiom: lift up His countenance toward you

meanings.meaning: For God to look on His people with a happy, kind face, showing that He is pleased with them and cares for them. It is like warm sunlight shining on them.

idioms.idiom: Is the LORD's arm too short?

meanings.meaning: God asks if His power has grown too weak to reach far enough. Nothing is too hard for Him, and Moses will soon see His promise come true.

idioms.idiom: they will be like bread for us

meanings.meaning: The people of the land will be easy to defeat, like bread that is eaten up. Their fields and goods would also give Israel plenty of food.
In Judges 6:16, God promises Gideon he will defeat all the Midianites together and as easily as if they were just one man, so that none are left.
In Judges 20, the Israelites acted all together with one mind, agreeing and joining as if they were a single person.

idioms.idiom: You have taken too much upon yourselves!

meanings.meaning: Literally "too much for you." The people accuse Moses and Aaron of grabbing more power than they deserve, since they say everyone is holy.
Moses says you have gone too far, claiming a holy job that was not yours. He uses the same words the rebels had said to him and Aaron.

idioms.idiom: bear the iniquity involving the sanctuary

meanings.meaning: The priests and Levites would be held responsible for anything wrong at God's holy place, including things that made it unfit for worship. They had to take the blame and make things right.
A promise that lasts forever and cannot be broken. Salt keeps food from spoiling, and sharing a meal with salt was seen as a pledge of loyal friendship.
The Levites were responsible for doing their work at the Tent of Meeting carefully. If they were careless or let people come in who should not, they would be blamed and take the punishment.

idioms.idiom: Aaron will be gathered to his people

meanings.meaning: It is a gentle way of saying Aaron would die. God told him this would happen on Mount Hor, and the same words are used for both good and bad people.

idioms.idiom: Water will flow from his buckets

meanings.meaning: Israel will have plenty of water, which in that hot land meant great blessing. Bible teachers picture it as a man carrying full buckets, or as water drawn for fields, or as rain from God.

idioms.idiom: A star will come forth from Jacob, and a scepter will arise from Israel

meanings.meaning: A great king would one day rise from Israel, since a star and a king's staff showed royal glory and power. Bible teachers say it points first to David, then to God's promised king.

idioms.idiom: Why should the name of our father disappear from his clan

meanings.meaning: The daughters ask why their father's family name and share of land should be lost just because he had no sons. They want to inherit so his place among his people continues.

idioms.idiom: go out and come in before them

meanings.meaning: To lead the people in everything they do, like a shepherd guiding his flock. Bible teachers say it may mean leading them in war and peace, or simply ruling them well.

idioms.idiom: will go out and come in

meanings.meaning: It means Joshua and all the people would act, going out and coming in, only as God directed. God's answer came through the high priest Eleazar, who asked counsel for Joshua using the Urim.
If a husband waits and then cancels his wife's promise to God, the guilt for the broken promise is put on him instead of her, and he must face the punishment.
Egypt is compared to a very hot furnace for melting iron. Life there was harsh, painful slavery for Israel, but God took His people out of it.
"All flesh" means people, human beings. In Deuteronomy it asks what person anywhere has ever heard God's voice from the fire and lived.
God punishes those who hate Him openly and quickly, without putting it off. Bible teachers say this may mean in their own lifetime, or right before Him, since they sin boldly.
Stubborn and unwilling to obey God. Stiff-necked people keep rebelling against Him and will not accept His commands, like an animal that refuses the yoke.

idioms.idiom: The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth beneath you iron

meanings.meaning: This describes a long drought. The sky is like hard bronze with no rain or dew, so the ground turns hard as iron and nothing can be plowed or grown, and God sends it.

idioms.idiom: the watered land as well as the dry

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean sin piles on sin, like adding fuel to a fire already burning, so a person who gives in to his wants only wants more.
Moses can no longer lead the people, such as guiding them out and in or going to battle. This did not mean he was too weak to move around.
To be the apple of His eye is to be guarded very carefully by God. Here God led Israel safely through the dangerous wilderness and protected His special people.
Israel is compared to a pampered animal that gets spoiled by good food and kind treatment and turns wild. When they had plenty, they became proud, lived for pleasure, and rebelled against God.
To have so much olive oil that you could dip your foot in it. It means Asher's land would be very fertile and rich, though some think it may point to pressing oil by foot.

idioms.idiom: rolled away the reproach of Egypt

meanings.meaning: God took away a shame from Israel. Bible teachers aren't sure which one: being uncircumcised, as the Egyptians were, Egyptians mocking them, or being slaves.

idioms.idiom: from the hand of the LORD

meanings.meaning: God Himself gave Jerusalem her punishment, and it is now finished. Bible teachers disagree about "double," which may mean full punishment or twice the blessing.

idioms.idiom: going the way of all the earth

meanings.meaning: Joshua means he is about to die. Death is a road every person on earth must walk, and Joshua is nearly at the end of his life.
To turn your heart fully toward the LORD, loving and fearing Him. Bible teachers disagree whether the foreign gods were real idols or things people loved more than God.
It means they died and were buried. Most of the people who lived in Joshua's time were gone, though a few may still have been alive, and a new generation came along.

idioms.idiom: Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna already in your possession

meanings.meaning: The leaders of Succoth mocked Gideon, asking if he had already captured these two kings. They doubted he would win and feared the kings' revenge, so they refused to feed his tired army.

idioms.idiom: If you had not plowed with my heifer

meanings.meaning: Samson means they used his wife, like a young cow pulling a plow, to get the answer. They did not solve the riddle on their own.
It means the whole land of Israel, from Dan in the far north to Beersheba in the far south. It points to people from all across the land.

idioms.idiom: the ears of all who hear it will tingle

meanings.meaning: God was about to do something so terrible that everyone who heard about it would be filled with horror and shock. The words would seem to ring in their ears.

idioms.idiom: His hand is heavy upon us

meanings.meaning: God was punishing the Philistines hard. They felt the weight of His power as death and trouble struck their city and showed their god Dagon was not stronger than Him.

idioms.idiom: Israel has become a stench to the Philistines

meanings.meaning: Israel had become hated by the Philistines. Saul's attack made them so angry that the Israelites' name seemed to "stink" to them, and they wanted revenge.

idioms.idiom: a man after His own heart

meanings.meaning: Someone God chose because he fit what God wanted and would do His will, unlike Saul. Adam Clarke says this is about how he led God's people as king, not about his private life.
His eyes became clear and lively again. Hunger and tiredness make the eyes look dull and dim, but after Jonathan ate the honey, his eyes brightened.
"The house of David" means David's family, not just David himself. Jonathan made this covenant for his own descendants too, so that both families would treat each other kindly.

idioms.idiom: march in and out with me

meanings.meaning: It means all of David's behavior as a soldier with Achish. Achish was saying David had acted well in the army and he could find nothing wrong with him.

idioms.idiom: Your blood be on your own head

meanings.meaning: David was saying the man himself was to blame for his own death. The man had said he killed the king, so he had to take the punishment for what he admitted.

idioms.idiom: the bow of Jonathan did not retreat

meanings.meaning: Jonathan's bow did not turn back until it had struck down mighty enemies. Bible teachers aren't sure, though, and one note says the fallen may be Israelites, and Jonathan kept fighting anyway.

idioms.idiom: the house of Saul and the house of David

meanings.meaning: These phrases mean the followers of each man: Saul's side, led by his son Ish-bosheth, and David's side. They fought a long war, and David's side grew stronger while Saul's grew weaker.

idioms.idiom: Am I the head of a dog

meanings.meaning: Abner is angrily asking, "Do you think I am a worthless, low creature?" He felt insulted, since he had been loyal to Saul's family.

idioms.idiom: May it whirl over the head of Joab

meanings.meaning: David wishes a terrible punishment would land on Joab and his family, so someone in it would always be sick, weak, killed, or hungry. One teacher says it was a prophecy of God's anger.

idioms.idiom: led Israel out and brought them back

meanings.meaning: Even when Saul was king, David was Israel's real leader. He led the army out to fight and brought the soldiers home safely, and Keil and Delitzsch say it also means he ran Israel's affairs.
God says that if David's son does wrong, He will correct him with ordinary human punishment, like troubles brought by people. He will still treat him as a son, and his kingdom won't be destroyed.

idioms.idiom: they would extinguish my one remaining ember

meanings.meaning: The woman's last son is like one glowing coal left from a fire. If he is killed, her last hope is gone, and her husband's name and family line would be wiped out.
Abishai insults Shimei by calling him a "dead dog." Calling him a dog shows he is seen as vile and shameless, with words like a dog's snarling, and "dead" means useless and hateful.

idioms.idiom: at the blast of the breath of His nostrils

meanings.meaning: This pictures God's anger like a powerful blast of wind from His nose. His angry warning was so mighty that the sea floor and the earth's foundations were uncovered.

idioms.idiom: the blood of the men who risked their lives

meanings.meaning: David said the water was like the men's blood because they risked their lives to get it. Drinking it would feel like drinking their blood, so he refused and poured it out to the LORD.

idioms.idiom: go the way of all the earth

meanings.meaning: This is a gentle way of saying "I am about to die." Everyone on earth, kings and ordinary people alike, must someday take this path to the grave.
It means David died, just as his ancestors had before him. He was not buried beside them, so it means he joined them among the dead.

idioms.idiom: at the expense of his life

meanings.meaning: Solomon meant that Adonijah would be put to death because of what he had asked for. Solomon saw the request as a new act of rebellion against him as king.
Solomon asks God, by His Spirit, to help the people want to love, respect, serve, and obey Him, following all the laws He gave their fathers.
People who pass by will make a hissing sound to show scorn. They will mock the people of Israel and be glad that Israel fell.

idioms.idiom: I will scourge you with scorpions

meanings.meaning: The king threatens to be much harsher than his father. Scorpions were probably whips with sharp iron points that tore the skin, though Bible teachers also say they may just mean rougher, crueler treatment.
The ten tribes were saying they would no longer follow Rehoboam or David's family. They would leave and go home, since they felt they would get nothing good from that king.

idioms.idiom: as one burns up dung until it is gone

meanings.meaning: God says He will completely sweep away Jeroboam's family, like people clear out dung (animal poop) until none is left. Jeroboam's family was as disgusting to Him as dung is to people.
Elisha says he is God's prophet and servant, who stands ready to serve the living LORD. He refuses the gift to show the healing came from God, and he was not acting for money.
These prophets were fed from Queen Jezebel's own kitchen. They did not sit at her royal table, but she supported them, so they were part of her household.

idioms.idiom: The one putting on his armor should not boast like one taking it off

meanings.meaning: Don't brag about winning before the battle is over. Someone who is just getting ready to fight shouldn't boast like someone who has already won, because no one knows how a war will end.

idioms.idiom: the chariots and horsemen of Israel

meanings.meaning: A cry of grief for a prophet who protected Israel better than an army could. Through his prayers and teaching from God, he did more for the nation than all its chariots and horsemen.

idioms.idiom: He used to pour water on the hands of Elijah

meanings.meaning: Elisha was Elijah's servant, since pouring water over a master's hands to wash was a common servant's job. The servant is saying Elisha was a true prophet who could tell them God's will.

idioms.idiom: even if the LORD were to make windows in heaven

meanings.meaning: The officer meant that even if God opened the sky and poured down food, this could not happen. Bible teachers disagree on whether he was mocking God or just saying it would take a miracle.

idioms.idiom: Tuck your cloak under your belt

meanings.meaning: This means to get ready to move fast. Long, loose robes were pulled up and tucked in at the waist so the man could travel quickly, because the task needed hurry.

idioms.idiom: children have come to the point of birth, but there is no strength to deliver them

meanings.meaning: A saying for a desperate crisis. Like a mother in labor who is too weak to push her baby out, the people had reached the critical moment but had no strength to get through it.
Hezekiah asks God to bend down His ear and really listen to his prayer. Piling up words like "hear" and "see" shows how earnestly he begs God for help.
It means Hezekiah died, just as his fathers before him had died. After that, his son Manasseh became king in his place.
Reuben lay with Bilhah, his father Jacob's concubine. Because of this sin, he lost the firstborn's special rights, and they went to Joseph's sons.

idioms.idiom: How can I drink the blood of these men who risked their lives?

meanings.meaning: David felt the water was so costly that drinking it would be like drinking the blood of the men who risked their lives to get it. He cared too much about them to drink it.

idioms.idiom: a spear like a weaver's beam

meanings.meaning: This describes the weapon of a giant Egyptian who stood about eight feet tall. His size and armor remind us of Goliath, and Benaiah's fight with him is a bit like David's.
This means a very large, powerful army. Some notes compare it to God's army of angels in heaven.
A promise that lasts forever and can never be broken. Salt keeps food from spoiling, and it was used in sacrifices when agreements were made, so God's promise to David's family would never end.
It means worshiping idols instead of God. God's people were seen as joined to Him like a wife to her husband, so serving other gods was like being unfaithful to Him.
Weak, frail human beings, who can't compare to God. Hezekiah says the Assyrians have only people to depend on, but God Himself is with His people to help them and fight for them.
To help and encourage them so they could keep working. God turned the king's heart toward them, and he let them go on building the temple and helped them until it was finished.
God's own people, the Israelites. He had set them apart from other nations as holy and chosen them to serve and worship Him, but marrying foreigners mixed them with the nations around them.
A saying that a person will give up everything he owns to save his life. Satan claims Job stayed faithful only because he was unharmed, and would turn from God if hurt.
Trapped by God with no way out. Job feels like a lost traveler walled in on every side, unable to escape or see where to go.
People's bodies, which are like houses where their souls live. Made of dust, they are weak and easily crushed, like a moth.
God will not help people who keep on doing evil. The Hebrew words mean He will not "take them by the hand" to lift them up when they fall.

idioms.idiom: lift up your hands to Him

meanings.meaning: To hold out your open hands to God in prayer. In this verse it goes with turning your heart toward Him and asking Him for help.

idioms.idiom: you are the people with whom wisdom itself will die

meanings.meaning: Job is being sarcastic. He mocks his friends as if they were the only wise people in the world, so that wisdom would disappear when they die.

idioms.idiom: fill his belly with the hot east wind

meanings.meaning: Eliphaz asks if a wise man would fill himself with stormy, empty wind. He means Job's words are like a storm: noisy and forceful, but empty and of no real use.

idioms.idiom: He gnashes His teeth at me

meanings.meaning: Job feels someone is attacking him in fierce anger, like a wild beast grinding its teeth at him. Bible teachers disagree on who it is: God, Job's friend Eliphaz, or Satan.

idioms.idiom: They have turned night into day

meanings.meaning: Most Bible teachers think Job means his friends call his dark time bright and say good days are near, even as death closes in. Adam Clarke instead sees Job's own gloomy thoughts.
The gates of Sheol are the way into the grave, the place of the dead, so going there means dying. In Job, it may mean his hopes or his body go down.
It pictures death as a parent whose "firstborn" is its most important child. Bible teachers differ: it may be the deadliest disease death ever produced, or a sudden blow that kills.
Most Bible teachers understand this as Death, shown as a fearsome ruler the wicked person is finally taken to. Adam Clarke disagrees and thinks it means a king of destruction.

idioms.idiom: injustice is broken like a tree

meanings.meaning: The wicked person, or maybe what he desires, is broken like a tree and ruined for good. Bible teachers describe it as a rotting tree that snaps easily, or as total, hopeless ruin.

idioms.idiom: It claps its hands at him and hisses him out of his place

meanings.meaning: Clapping and hissing show scorn as the wicked man is driven from his place. Bible teachers differ on who does it: people glad at his ruin, or a storm acting like a crowd.
When God hides His face, He is not seen. The notes say this may happen to a guilty nation or to one person, and no one can say He is unjust.
The wicked lose their strength to do harm. An arm raised to hurt someone falls down powerless when morning light ends their dark deeds.

idioms.idiom: tilt the water jars of the heavens

meanings.meaning: The clouds are pictured as skin water bottles in the sky. Only God can empty them to pour out rain, and no one can stop Him when He does.
A kiss was how subjects honored their king, so this means to honor and obey the King God chose. Bible teachers aren't sure of the word "Son"; it may mean "chosen one."

idioms.idiom: Shine the light of Your face upon us

meanings.meaning: The writer asks God to look on His people with a happy, kind face. It means showing His favor and love, so their hearts fill with trust, hope, and joy.
Their mouths are like open graves. Bible teachers say it pictures people whose words are cruel and deadly, like a grave that is hungry to swallow others, or an open grave whose breath is foul.
The writer asks God to let wicked people be ruined by their own plans, like falling into a pit they dug for others. Haman was hanged on the wooden frame he prepared for Mordecai.
Like a woman giving birth, a wicked person works hard to bring about evil. He plans trouble, but what he produces is lies, and his hopes are ruined.
A cry for God to use His power and act. The notes say it may mean He should stop the wicked, and punish them if they won't change.
To "incline your ear" means to bend your ear toward a speaker and listen closely. Here, a teacher asks you to listen to wise words, ready to learn, and then think them over.
A double heart means seeming to have two hearts: one speaks nice words while the other plans something else. These people say one thing but mean another, so you can't trust them.
Evil people hurt and ruin God's people without any pity, as easily and as often as they eat bread. They feel no guilt about it.
David asks God to lean in close and listen carefully to his prayer, like someone bending down to hear a person who is weak or speaking softly. He trusts that God will hear and answer.
The apple of the eye is the part of the eye people guard most carefully. David asks God to protect him that carefully, because God's people are dear to Him.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean people mock the wicked with a head shake, or it may mean they flee in fear that the same will happen to them.
To be dying or heading for the grave. Clarke says every dying person will trust in Christ, since no one can keep his own soul alive.

idioms.idiom: lift up his soul to an idol

meanings.meaning: To love and be loyal to an idol or something false instead of God. The person who may come near to God does not do this and keeps his promises honestly.

idioms.idiom: Lift up your heads, O gates

meanings.meaning: The gates are told to open wide so the King of Glory, the LORD, can come in. Bible teachers differ on which place is meant, such as the temple.
David feels forgotten, like a dead person no one thinks about anymore. Bible teachers differ: Gill says friends or God forgot him, while Clarke says he was treated like someone sentenced to die.
He was so scared that he felt God had turned away from him and would no longer protect him, as if his case was hopeless. But God heard his cry for help anyway.
To wink with the eye is a rude, insulting sign that shows spite toward someone. David asks God not to let people who hate him for no reason treat him this way.
Evildoers will be removed from the earth, like branches cut from a tree. They may do well for a while, but in the end they will be gone.
To grind your teeth at someone shows fierce anger and hatred, like a wild animal in a rage. Here the wicked are full of this anger toward good people while they plot against them.
God has made the speaker ready to listen to Him and obey. Bible teachers aren't sure if this points to piercing a servant's ear to show lifelong service, or just to hearing as obeying.
One trouble comes right after another, like ocean waves crashing one on top of the next. The writer feels completely covered by his sorrows.
Other nations use Israel as an example of misery and punishment, and they mock them with sayings like "May you end up like them!"
The king speaks with a special gift of charming, powerful words. This gift is given to him, and it becomes a source of strength and a blessing.
The oil of joy is oil put on someone at happy feasts and special times. Being anointed with it means God honored this king with gladness above the other kings.
To "see decay" means to stay in the grave until the body rots. God promised His Holy One, Jesus, would not stay dead in the grave, because God would raise Him up.

idioms.idiom: They devour my people like bread

meanings.meaning: Wicked people hurt and destroy God's people as easily and carelessly as they eat bread. They are cruel like wild animals that hunt, and they don't call on God at all.
David asks that his enemies die suddenly and while still strong, not slowly. Gill and Calvin say it may echo Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, whom the earth swallowed alive.
The writer will be up at daybreak to praise God, showing great eagerness. Bible teachers read it as him waking the morning with his song, or as him waking early himself.
Even the lowest, most despised people, like drunkards, made him the subject of their jokes and mocking talk. Important men at the town gate spoke against him too.

idioms.idiom: May their table become a snare

meanings.meaning: The good things the enemies enjoy, like food and feeling safe, would be turned by God into a trap that brings them down. Teachers differ on whether it is a prayer or a prediction.
It means the king's enemies will be so completely beaten that they end up in the lowest position, like humble servants. Adam Clarke says they will be reduced to that state.
Wicked people wear their pride all around them, like a chain around the neck. Bible teachers add that they may think it makes them look great, or that pride holds them like a prisoner.
To talk in a proud, stuck-up, bossy way, as if you are better than everyone. Gill says it means speaking arrogantly and harshly, with a stiff neck held up high.
This is the manna God sent from heaven. The Hebrew says "bread of the mighty," so Bible teachers explain it as either food of angels or rich food fit for princes.
A faulty bow can't be trusted, because it may drop the arrow, send it the wrong way, or snap back. Israel turned away from God and let Him down, just like their fathers.

idioms.idiom: cause Your face to shine upon us

meanings.meaning: A prayer asking God to show He is pleased with His people again. They want Him to be kind and near to them, as if He were smiling on them, so they can be saved.
Being right and having peace come together like friends who meet and hug. Bible teachers explain it differently: God's mercy and justice agreeing, or God's peace meeting faithful people.
To pray to God with your whole heart, sincerely and eagerly, trusting Him and wanting His help.
A lifted-up horn here points to strength and honor that come from God's favor. Bible teachers say His people grow stronger, wiser and happier, and some think the horn means Christ.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean asking God to help us see how short life is so we live wisely, or it may be about learning the power of His anger.
The abode of silence is the quiet of the grave, where the dead are. The writer says that without the LORD's help he would soon have died.
It means Israel was unfaithful to God by worshiping idols. God's people were like a wife promised to Him, so idol worship broke that promise.
Bible teachers disagree. Some say the dew means the king's young men, who come to him gladly like fresh morning dew, while others say it means the king's own youthful strength.

idioms.idiom: his horn will be lifted high in honor

meanings.meaning: A person's "horn" stands for their power and strength. This kind, giving man will be lifted up with honor, so people will respect him and stop looking down on him.

idioms.idiom: like a wineskin dried up by smoke

meanings.meaning: A wine bottle made of animal skin gets black, dry and shriveled when it hangs in smoke. The writer feels worn out and useless from suffering and sorrow.

idioms.idiom: the shade on your right hand

meanings.meaning: God is like cool shade right beside you, covering you from the sun's burning heat. He stays close at your side to protect and defend you.

idioms.idiom: whose quiver is full of them

meanings.meaning: A quiver holds arrows, so a full quiver pictures a house full of children, who help a father stand strong against his enemies. Clarke thought it might mean the wife.

idioms.idiom: The plowmen plowed over my back

meanings.meaning: Enemies treated Israel cruelly, as if plowing its back like a field. Bible teachers aren't sure if it means whipping or being tied to a plow and made to pull it.
Grass on a flat roof doesn't get enough nourishment, so it dries up before it grows. The verse asks that enemies of God's people become like this, good for nothing.

idioms.idiom: may my right hand cease to function

meanings.meaning: The writer says that if he ever forgets Jerusalem, may he lose the use of his right hand. Adam Clarke links this to losing his skill at playing the harp.
It means being right at the edge of the grave. Bible teachers aren't sure if it pictures people killed and left unburied, or David's men feeling hopeless and close to death.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean people who break their promises and agreements, whose boasts of power are empty, or who do wicked things with their hands.

idioms.idiom: incline your ear to my sayings

meanings.meaning: To lean in and listen carefully. The speaker is a father teaching his son, and he wants him to treat these words as very important.
Wormwood is a very bitter plant. The verse means that what sounds sweet at first, like the honey in the lines before it, ends in something bitter: loss, hurt, and sorrow.
The "fountain" most likely means a man's wife, and the wish is that she be blessed, perhaps with children, and that he be happy with her. Clarke reads it as a picture of the body.
A sneaky, dishonest person sends secret signals with his feet, like pressing someone's foot or scraping the ground, to tell others what to do without speaking out loud.
Winking is a sly signal from someone up to no good. He may be tricking, secretly plotting against, or mocking others, and it brings sorrow to them and to himself.
Someone who causes trouble in his own family will end up with nothing worth having, like trying to hold the wind. What he gets is empty, or he loses it.
The words a person speaks are like fruit that grows from his mouth. Good words bring good things back to the one who speaks them, just as a farmer gets to eat his own fruit.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean the lovely things and light the eyes see, like nature and the sun, or whatever gives light to guide us, and it makes the heart glad.
Pressing or biting the lips is a sign of a sly, unkind person who has already made up his mind to do something bad. It shows he is set on his wicked plan.
Bible teachers aren't sure. He may shut his eyes to think hard about evil plans, or wink to secretly signal friends about them.
Shaking hands was how people long ago sealed a deal. Here, a person shakes hands to promise to pay a friend's debt if the friend doesn't pay, and the proverb calls this unwise.
A wicked person eagerly does wrong, as if it were food they enjoy. Like a hungry man gulping down a meal, he does evil greedily and with pleasure.

idioms.idiom: The spirit of a man is the lamp of the LORD

meanings.meaning: God gives each person a spirit, or mind and conscience, that works like a lamp He lit inside. It shines into the hidden parts of a person's heart, helping them know right from wrong.

idioms.idiom: The king's heart is a waterway in the hand of the LORD

meanings.meaning: A king's heart is like a stream of water in God's hand. Just as a farmer can turn water into any channel, God can turn a king's thoughts and choices wherever He wants.

idioms.idiom: A wicked man hardens his face

meanings.meaning: A wicked person puts on a bold, shameless look. He doesn't blush or feel sorry for his sins, and he ignores correction and stubbornly does what he wants.

idioms.idiom: put a knife to your throat

meanings.meaning: It means to hold yourself back and control your appetite when eating with a ruler. Some Bible teachers also see it as watching your words, or remembering that the table could be dangerous.

idioms.idiom: heap burning coals on his head

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean that kindness to an enemy is the strongest kind of payback, like a punishment from God, but Gill says it is not meant to hurt him.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean lips that speak warm words of love and friendship while the heart is wicked, or lips burning with angry, hateful words.

idioms.idiom: The wounds of a friend are faithful

meanings.meaning: A real friend may hurt you by pointing out your faults, but he does it out of love and for your good. An enemy's kisses may look kind, but they cannot be trusted.
This means a person looks away on purpose so he won't see poor people's needs or have to help. Because he refuses to care, he will receive many curses.
God gives life, sunlight, and the good things of this world to both the poor person and the cheating one. He may also give some of each His special help.

idioms.idiom: She eats and wipes her mouth

meanings.meaning: A woman who is unfaithful to her husband hides what she did, like someone wiping their mouth after eating something they shouldn't. Then she acts innocent and says she did nothing wrong.
She gets ready for her work with energy and determination. People tucked up their long robes when they started serious work, so this shows she works hard and eagerly.
Here on earth, in this present life where people live and work, as opposed to the life to come. This phrase is found only in the book of Ecclesiastes.
Folding your hands means sitting idle and refusing to work. Bible teachers aren't sure what "eats his own flesh" means; it may mean he starves and harms his family, or that he torments himself.
Eating stands for the whole way a person lives, so his life is gloomy and joyless, full of worry about losing his money. One teacher thinks it may also mean he eats secretly at night.
It means people who are alive in this world. Wisdom helps them while they live on earth.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean wicked rulers came and went from the holy place or courts with great honor, or that they were sent from it to their graves.

idioms.idiom: Cast your bread upon the waters

meanings.meaning: Share what you have with people in need, even if it seems like throwing it away. Like a farmer's seed, it will come back to you later with plenty extra, as God rewards it.
To join hands with foreigners, such as by making alliances or marrying them. Bible teachers also think it may mean joining them in worship, or having children outside of marriage.
God was still angry and had not finished punishing His people. His arm stayed stretched out, ready to strike again, so even after all the trouble, more was still coming.
The two enemy kings are like burnt-out sticks of firewood that only give off smoke. Their anger looks scary, but they are weak, their rage is empty, and it won't last long.
God seems to turn away from His people and not show them His kindness or help, because He is judging them. Isaiah still trusts Him and waits for His kindness to return.
The coming King will defeat the wicked with just what comes from His mouth, like a breath or a spoken judgment. His words of judgment are enough to stop them.
It means the King's spoken words of judgment, which strike down the wicked like a rod. One Bible teacher thinks the word may really be "blast," like a breath.
People's hands go weak and hang down because they are so afraid. When God comes in judgment, the people of Babylon will have no courage or strength left to fight back.
People's courage melts away, like wax near a fire. They become so afraid and discouraged that they have no strength or will left to fight back or save themselves.
It means God is using His power to carry out what He has planned. Nothing and no one is strong enough to stop Him or make Him change course.

idioms.idiom: head or tail, palm or reed

meanings.meaning: Nobody in Egypt, from the highest to the lowest, can do anything to fix the trouble. God has left them so confused that no one's work succeeds.

idioms.idiom: the key to the house of David

meanings.meaning: The key is a sign of a job in charge of the king's household. Whoever carries it has full power to open and shut, deciding who may come in.
People felt as safe from death and the grave as if they had made a deal with them. Bible teachers aren't sure if this means a treaty with Assyria or something else.

idioms.idiom: You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble

meanings.meaning: God's enemies plan and work hard, but their efforts are useless, like the dry leftover bits of plants that people throw away. Their own pride and anger will end up destroying them like a fire.

idioms.idiom: your neck is iron and your forehead is bronze

meanings.meaning: God is saying His people are very stubborn. They won't bend to what He wants, and they feel no shame about their sin or accept correction for it.

idioms.idiom: Is My hand too short to redeem you

meanings.meaning: A short hand pictured weakness, and a long stretched-out hand pictured power. God asks if He has become too weak to save His people, but He is still strong enough to rescue them.
God's anger and punishment, pictured as a cup that made Jerusalem stagger like a drunk. Here God Himself takes the cup away, and she will never drink it again.
God has shown His mighty power openly, like a warrior who bares his arm to fight freely. Everyone in every nation can see how He saves His people.
People are like foolish sheep that wander from their shepherd, each going his own selfish way toward ruin. Bible teachers differ on who "we" means: all people, God's chosen people, or Israel.

idioms.idiom: ride on the heights of the land

meanings.meaning: God promises to make His people rulers of their land, like a warrior riding over its high hills and forts. Some teachers say it simply means He will bring them back home.
God's people will be fed and helped by other nations and their kings, like a baby nursed by its mother. Bible teachers say this means sharing their riches and support.
They threw off all God's rules and refused to be held back by them. Like an ox that breaks free of its yoke, these leaders would not obey God's law.
Their hands go weak and shaky with fear. When the people hear the enemy is coming, they lose their strength and feel too frightened to fight back.
To pay attention and be willing to listen. The people showed no wish to hear God's words and followed their own stubborn hearts instead.
To pay attention to God and listen so closely that you obey. The people ignored God's many warnings and followed their own stubborn, evil hearts instead.

idioms.idiom: the ears of all who hear of it will ring

meanings.meaning: God says He will bring a disaster so shocking and terrible that everyone who hears about it will be stunned, as if their ears were ringing.
These prophets spoke their own ideas, then claimed "The LORD declares it," though God had not spoken. Some teachers think they also flattered people with smooth words, but Calvin disagrees.
The nations will be so shaken by the terrible punishment God sends that they lose their good sense and act almost crazy, as if they were drunk.
Their hands hang weak because they are so scared. The fear is so great that fathers run to save themselves and don't even turn back to help their own children.
To suffer the punishment God gives, pictured as a cup to drink. Even people who deserved it less drank it, so Edom will not escape either.

idioms.idiom: without a hand turned to help her

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean no human hands worked against Sodom, since God Himself destroyed it in a moment, unlike Jerusalem, which suffered a long attack by enemy armies.
The king was like the people's breath, because their life and hope depended on him. The notes say this was Zedekiah, Judah's last king, caught by the Chaldeans.
Hearts that were unfaithful to God. The people left Him and chased after idols, like a husband or wife who breaks their promise to be faithful in marriage.

idioms.idiom: every knee will turn to water

meanings.meaning: People will be so terrified that their knees go weak, like water. Bible teachers differ: some say it means losing strength, and others say fear can make people lose control of their bladder.

idioms.idiom: putting the branch to their nose

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers aren't sure. It may be an act of idol worship, like holding a branch to the face while praying to the rising sun, or an insult that made God angry.

idioms.idiom: The city is the cooking pot, and we are the meat

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers aren't sure. The people may be mocking the warning that Jerusalem would be a boiling pot, or they may mean they will stay in the city no matter what happens.
Lifting a hand was the sign of swearing an oath. When God says this, He is making a serious promise, or a serious vow, and He means to keep it.
Everyone will be so afraid of the enemy army that they lose their courage, like wax melting. John Gill says this will even be true of people who laughed at the warning.
People's courage would fail because they were so afraid. John Gill says their hearts would lose strength at the sight of swords drawn at every gate, seeing nothing but death.
The broken wall is a picture of the people's sin. To stand in the gap is to plead with God for them and lead them back to Him, so He would not destroy the land.

idioms.idiom: set your face against the Ammonites

meanings.meaning: God told Ezekiel to turn toward the land of the Ammonites with a bold, stern look and speak against them, showing that God Himself was against them and would judge them.

idioms.idiom: The gate to the nations is broken

meanings.meaning: Jerusalem was like a busy gate where people from many nations came and went. Tyre cheered that it was broken, hoping the trade and wealth that went to Jerusalem would now come to Tyre.
God told Ezekiel to turn and look toward Sidon with a stern face and speak His warning against it. The message was that ruin was coming.
The people of Israel feel hopeless, like a branch cut off a tree or a limb cut off a body. They see nothing in themselves that could revive them.
This describes foreigners who had no circumcision, the body sign of belonging to God's people, and whose hearts did not follow God either. God said they could not enter His sanctuary.

idioms.idiom: the Messiah will be cut off

meanings.meaning: "Cut off" means the Messiah, God's chosen one, would be killed and would have nothing. These notes say this is Jesus, and that His death was followed by Jerusalem's destruction.
It means Israel was unfaithful to God, like a wife who cheats on her husband. The notes say this was idolatry, worshipping idols instead of the living God, which broke her promise to Him.

idioms.idiom: they have played the harlot against their God

meanings.meaning: The people turned away from God to worship idols. God was like a husband to them, so leaving Him for idols was like a wife being unfaithful to her husband.

idioms.idiom: The whirlwind has wrapped them in its wings

meanings.meaning: It may be a picture of a sudden storm sweeping Israel away from their land. Some teachers think it pictures their false worship as useless, like trying to catch the wind.
Moving a boundary stone meant stealing a neighbor's land by breaking the limits that kept things fair. Judah's leaders broke God's limits of right, so He would pour out His anger.
Ephraim is like a cake burned on one side and raw on the other, so it is useless. Bible teachers aren't sure if it means a half-hearted people or a partly punished one.

idioms.idiom: Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting?

meanings.meaning: God promises to save His people from death and the grave, then asks where their plagues and sting are, as if death has lost its power. Some teachers see a threat instead.

idioms.idiom: For three transgressions of Damascus, even four

meanings.meaning: The numbers aren't an exact count. "Three, even four" means sin piled on sin, again and again, so God will not take back His punishment of Damascus.

idioms.idiom: For three transgressions of Israel, even four

meanings.meaning: This isn't an exact count. God is saying Israel sinned again and again, so He will not hold back His punishment, since judges let bribes, even tiny ones, decide against honest and poor people.
Having clean teeth because there was no food to chew. God sent hunger to their cities, as the next line, "lack of bread," explains.

idioms.idiom: like a firebrand snatched from a blaze

meanings.meaning: A burning stick pulled out of the fire just in time. It means some people barely escaped being destroyed, yet they still did not turn back to God.
Judges and leaders twist fair judgment into something bitter. Justice should be sweet and good, but they make it as harsh and unpleasant as wormwood, a bitter plant, by being unfair to people.
David's royal family and kingdom had fallen so low that it was like a broken-down tent. God promises to lift it up and rebuild it, a promise the notes link to the Messiah, David's descendant.

idioms.idiom: so all the nations will drink continually

meanings.meaning: Drinking pictures facing God's punishment, like a cup of His anger. Bible teachers aren't sure if "you" means Edom or Israel, but all nations will drink it too.
Sheol is the unseen world of the dead, like a grave or deep pit. Jonah says he cried out from its belly because the fish, deep in the sea, felt like Sheol.

idioms.idiom: cannot tell their right hand from their left

meanings.meaning: This describes very young children, who don't yet know even simple things like left from right. God points out that Nineveh had many such innocent children, so He cared about the city.
A poetic name for Jerusalem and its people, pictured as a daughter. Here Lachish is said to be where sin began that then spread to Jerusalem.
A man who claims to speak for God but is really full of empty, lying words. He tells people the nice things they want to hear, like promises of plenty of wine and drink.

idioms.idiom: walk in the name of their gods

meanings.meaning: To live following and worshiping a god. The other nations each follow their own gods, but God's people promise to keep worshiping the LORD faithfully, trusting His promises, forever.

idioms.idiom: let us feast our eyes on Zion

meanings.meaning: The enemy nations wanted to stare at Zion (Jerusalem) while it was shamed and hurt. They would enjoy seeing her suffer instead of feeling sorry for her.

idioms.idiom: seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men

meanings.meaning: It means a full, big enough number of leaders. When Assyria attacks, God's people will have plenty of shepherds, or rulers, to stand against the enemy, though some teachers think it points to real leaders.

idioms.idiom: the stones will cry out from the wall

meanings.meaning: The stones and beams of a house built by stealing and hurting people are pictured as speaking up against the builder. Even his walls would cry out for God to punish the wrong.

idioms.idiom: they rose early to corrupt all their deeds

meanings.meaning: God hoped His people would learn from His correction, but instead they became even more eager to do wrong, rushing to do it like people who get up early.

idioms.idiom: do not let your hands fall limp

meanings.meaning: Don't be afraid or lose heart. God's people are told to keep doing His work and not give up.

idioms.idiom: lifted up their horns against the land of Judah

meanings.meaning: Lifting a horn means acting proud and tough because you feel strong. These nations used their power to bully Judah and scatter its people, but God will send workers to throw those horns down.

idioms.idiom: sit under your own vine and fig tree

meanings.meaning: It pictures a calm, safe life with nothing to fear, when God's people have enough and neighbors can meet together in peace. God promises this change will come suddenly, "in that day."
A time when a work has only a small, weak start. People looked down on the rebuilding of the temple, but God watches over it with favor and will see it finished.
Be brave and keep going. God tells His people to take courage and not give up, because He has promised good things, so they can keep building the temple and not be afraid.

idioms.idiom: this magnificent price at which they valued me

meanings.meaning: God calls the price "magnificent" even though it was really a tiny payment of thirty pieces of silver. It shows how little the people valued the shepherd's work.

idioms.idiom: living water will flow out from Jerusalem

meanings.meaning: Fresh, flowing water pours out of Jerusalem toward the east and the west and never dries up, all year long. Bible teachers say it pictures God's life-giving knowledge and salvation spreading out to the world.
"Hated" here means God did not love Esau the way He loved Jacob, and did not choose him for special favor. Esau's land was left ruined.
People who see that they are spiritually needy and cannot help themselves. It is not only about having little money, and the kingdom of heaven belongs to them.

idioms.idiom: not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen

meanings.meaning: Not even the tiniest part of God's Law will be dropped. A jot is the smallest Hebrew letter, and Jesus is saying every little detail will last until everything it points to has come true.

idioms.idiom: if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away

meanings.meaning: Jesus uses a shocking picture to show how serious sin is. Even losing a hand, the body part that acts, would be better than ending up in hell.

idioms.idiom: Eye for eye and tooth for tooth

meanings.meaning: This old law said a punishment should match the harm done, and it was meant for judges, not for getting even yourself. Many Jewish teachers said the person paid the value of the loss instead.
Bible teachers aren't sure. "Good eyes" may mean a giving, generous heart, as Jewish people then used the words, or it may mean a heart aimed at one right goal.

idioms.idiom: The eye is the lamp of the body

meanings.meaning: Just as your eye lights the way for your body, what your heart is set on guides how you live. Teachers differ: it may mean aiming to please God alone, or being generous.

This describes the sad place of punishment for people shut out from God's kingdom. Weeping shows their deep pain, and gnashing of teeth, which means grinding the teeth, shows they feel there is no hope.

idioms.idiom: let the dead bury their own dead

meanings.meaning: Let people who are not following God take care of burying the dead. Burying a father is a good thing, but Jesus had called this man to a more important job, serving Him.

idioms.idiom: No one sews a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment

meanings.meaning: Mixing new with old can make things worse. Teachers disagree: Calvin says Jesus was easing His followers into fasting; Gill says fasting just didn't suit them while He was with them.

idioms.idiom: We played the flute for you, and you did not dance

meanings.meaning: Jesus compares people to children whose friends won't join any game, happy or sad. Those people were never pleased, whether John came strict or Jesus came eating and drinking with others.

idioms.idiom: It is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to the dogs

meanings.meaning: Jesus used a saying of His day to test the woman's faith. The "children" were the Jews, the "bread" was His teaching and miracles, and "dogs" meant people who weren't Jewish.

idioms.idiom: Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees

meanings.meaning: Jesus was not talking about real bread. "Leaven" (yeast) stood for the wrong teachings of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and He warned His followers to stay away from them.

idioms.idiom: Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven

meanings.meaning: Jesus gives all twelve apostles, not just Peter, a say in who belongs to the church and who is put out. Heaven stands behind the choices they make on earth.

idioms.idiom: If your hand or your foot causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away

meanings.meaning: Jesus says to refuse anything that makes you stumble into sin, even if giving it up costs a lot. Staying out of the eternal fire is worth far more.

idioms.idiom: Can you drink the cup I am going to drink?

meanings.meaning: Jesus asks if James and John can go through the same hard suffering He is about to face. They had asked for honor, but did not understand what it would cost.

idioms.idiom: You strain out a gnat but swallow a camel

meanings.meaning: Jesus says the leaders fuss over tiny rules but ignore huge wrongs. They strained drinks to avoid a gnat, yet it was like swallowing a camel, the biggest animal they knew.

idioms.idiom: Fill up, then, the measure of the sin of your fathers

meanings.meaning: Jesus was not really telling the leaders to do evil. He was warning that they would finish what their ancestors began, filling their sin to the top by killing God's Son and His messengers.

idioms.idiom: Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather

meanings.meaning: Calvin and Gill disagree about this. Gill says the dead body means the Jewish people in their ruined state, while Calvin says Christ is calling His children to gather to Him.

idioms.idiom: if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it

meanings.meaning: The "cup" stands for the suffering and death Jesus was about to face. He says that if it cannot be avoided, He is willing to go through it, because He wants His Father's will done.

idioms.idiom: sitting at the right hand of Power

meanings.meaning: "Power" is a name for God, who is all-powerful. Jesus says people will see Him sitting at God's right hand, which proves He is the Son of God.

idioms.idiom: His blood be on us and on our children

meanings.meaning: The crowd asked that the blame and punishment for Jesus' death fall on them and their children. They accepted the guilt if there was any wrong in killing Him.
"Fallen asleep" is a gentle way of saying these believers had died. The notes say they were God's people whose bodies lay in the graves, and they were raised to life.

idioms.idiom: He is out of His mind

meanings.meaning: His family said Jesus was acting crazy, so they wanted to take Him home. Bible teachers differ: they may have truly thought His mind was confused, or only worried He was too tired.

idioms.idiom: If your hand causes you to sin, cut it off

meanings.meaning: Jesus doesn't mean to hurt your body. He means to give up anything that leads you to sin, even something as dear as a hand, because that is better than losing life.

idioms.idiom: everyone will be salted with fire

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers say this is a hard verse. The notes here explain it as hell's fire keeping the wicked from being destroyed, the way salt keeps meat from spoiling, so their punishment never ends.
The "cup" means the hard suffering and death Jesus saw coming. He asks the Father to take it away if He is willing, but He chooses to do what the Father wants.
A "horn of salvation" means a mighty Savior whom God raised up from David's family. Horns were a picture of strength, like the horns of strong animals.
People who give freely will get back a big, overflowing amount. Like a heaped-up measure, what comes back to them will be more than enough.
To "fall away" on account of Jesus means to be put off by Him and start to doubt or turn away from Him. Jesus says the person who does not doubt Him is blessed.
These people stop believing when trouble comes. Their faith lasted only a short time because it had no deep root, so it did not stay strong when tested.

idioms.idiom: Your eye is the lamp of your body

meanings.meaning: Your eyes show your body where to go, and your mind does the same for your life. When your mind is clear and set on God's truth, your whole life is filled with light.

Jesus warns His followers to watch out for the Pharisees' bad influence. Luke calls it hypocrisy, but Bible teachers aren't sure, since some think He meant their false teaching, and the Pharisees had both.

idioms.idiom: to ignite a fire on the earth

meanings.meaning: Bible teachers aren't sure what the fire is. It may be the good news and Spirit Jesus brings, which warm God's people and destroy sin, or the hard trouble people face for following Him.
A fox stood for a wicked ruler who was cunning and cruel. Jesus probably meant Herod, though Bible teachers aren't completely sure.

idioms.idiom: your house is left to you desolate

meanings.meaning: Jesus says the temple, and maybe the whole city, will soon be left empty and ruined. He says "your" house, not His, because He has left it.
To patiently and gladly accept whatever hard things come from following Jesus, like shame, trouble, or even death. Anyone who won't do this isn't truly His disciple.
It means being right beside Abraham after death. Lazarus is pictured as lying next to him, like a guest at the heavenly feast.
God invites Jesus, David's Lord, to sit at His right side in heaven. This shows Jesus was raised up and given authority, as God made Him Lord.
God will completely defeat Jesus' enemies and put them under His control. Long ago, conquerors put their feet on the necks of beaten leaders to show they had lost all their power.

idioms.idiom: sift all of you like wheat

meanings.meaning: Satan asked God's permission to test all the disciples hard, as he did with Job. Sifting shakes grain to separate wheat from chaff, and Satan hoped to find little real faith.

idioms.idiom: seated at the right hand of the power of God

meanings.meaning: Jesus says He will sit beside God in a place of honor and power. Gill says this began after Jesus rose from the dead and went up to heaven.

idioms.idiom: if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?

meanings.meaning: Jesus uses a saying about trees. If this happens to Him, the innocent One, far worse will come to the guilty, which teachers link to hard times that later fell on the Jewish people.

idioms.idiom: My hour has not yet come

meanings.meaning: Jesus means the right time for Him to work a miracle had not fully come yet. He was doing His Father's work, so His mother could not tell Him when to do it.

idioms.idiom: Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up again

meanings.meaning: Jesus was speaking in a riddle about His own body. He was saying that if people killed Him, He would bring Himself back to life in three days, as a sign of His power.
The friend of the bridegroom is the helper who serves the groom at his wedding. John the Baptist used it of himself: Jesus is the groom, and John gladly serves Him.
Living water meant fresh, flowing spring water, not still water from a pond or tank. Jesus offered the woman something far better than well water, and it was a gift from God.
God the Father has clearly marked Jesus out as the one chosen for this special job: giving people the bread of life that lasts forever. His mark proves Jesus is truly sent by Him.

idioms.idiom: eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man

meanings.meaning: Jesus was not talking about really eating. He meant receiving what His death gives, as a body takes in food, and without this a person cannot be saved.

idioms.idiom: His hour had not yet come

meanings.meaning: The exact time God had set for Jesus to be arrested, suffer, and die had not come yet. Until then, no one could seize Him, even though they wanted to.
This is mostly understood to be Satan, who rules over people who stand against God. Jesus says His death defeats him, though one Bible teacher thought it meant Jesus Himself.

idioms.idiom: has lifted up his heel against Me

meanings.meaning: A close friend who shared Jesus' table turned against Him and treated Him badly. Jesus meant Judas, and Bible teachers differ on whether the Psalm first spoke of Ahithophel or Absalom.
A person headed for ruin, as if destruction were his parent. In John 17:12 it is Judas, who was lost, and in 2 Thessalonians 2:3 it is the wicked "man of lawlessness."

idioms.idiom: He is at my right hand

meanings.meaning: God is right beside Him, close and ready to help and protect Him, like a helper standing at His side to defend Him. So He will not be shaken.

idioms.idiom: to the right hand of God

meanings.meaning: Jesus was lifted up to the highest place of honor and power beside God in heaven. Bible teachers also note it may mean He was raised by God's mighty power.
People far away from the Jews Peter spoke to, like Jews living in other lands and Gentiles (non-Jews). The promise is for all whom God calls.

idioms.idiom: completely cut off from among his people

meanings.meaning: To be cut off from God's people and destroyed by God as a punishment. Anyone who refuses to listen to the Prophet God sent, who is Christ, would lose their place among God's people.
This means Jesus was killed by being hanged on a cross. Gill's notes say crucifixion was a shameful, painful way to die, and Jamieson-Fausset-Brown says it means 'killed by hanging.'

idioms.idiom: You stiff-necked people with uncircumcised hearts and ears

meanings.meaning: Stubborn like an ox that won't bend its neck to the yoke. Their hearts and ears were closed to God, so they would not listen or obey Him.

idioms.idiom: at the right hand of God

meanings.meaning: The right hand of a king was the place of honor, where someone shared in his power and glory. Jesus being at God's right hand shows He has the highest honor and authority.

idioms.idiom: You are out of your mind

meanings.meaning: "You're crazy!" The believers said this because her news that Peter was free sounded too good to be true, even though they had been praying for it.

idioms.idiom: a man after My own heart

meanings.meaning: God found David to be a king who would rule the way God wanted. One Bible teacher says this is about how David led the people by God's law, not about his private life.
Jesus' body was never left in the grave to rot. God raised Him to life so He would never die again, unlike others who were raised but died later.
To "see decay" means David died, was buried, and his body rotted in the grave. Unlike Jesus, whom God raised, David's body did not escape the grave's decay.
His body never rotted in the grave. God raised Jesus from the dead so soon that He did not decay, unlike David, who died, was buried, and decayed.
They put themselves in great danger, even of dying, for Jesus. Paul and Barnabas had already suffered much for Him, such as being driven out of a town and Paul being stoned.

idioms.idiom: Your blood be on your own heads!

meanings.meaning: Paul is saying that if these men face punishment for rejecting the message, it is their own fault, not his. They will have only themselves to blame for what happens to them.
It means the believers met to share the Lord's Supper, with bread standing for Christ's body. Clarke thinks they may also have shared a regular meal, but Gill says it was not just that.
Paul is calling the high priest a hypocrite. He sat as a judge to follow the law, but he broke the law by ordering Paul to be struck.

idioms.idiom: It is hard for you to kick against the goads

meanings.meaning: Jesus was scolding Saul for stubbornly resisting what he already felt was true in his heart. Saul was fighting against his own convictions on purpose.
"According to the flesh" means as a human being. As a man, Jesus came from King David's family, and the notes say He was also more than human.
"Walk" is an old way of describing how a person lives their life. To walk according to the flesh means to live by the pull of our own sinful desires, not by the Spirit.

idioms.idiom: put to death the deeds of the body

meanings.meaning: With the Holy Spirit's help, resist sinful desires and stop doing sinful things. Giving in to them leads to death, but resisting them leads to life with God.

idioms.idiom: How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news

meanings.meaning: People who tell the good news about God's gifts and peace are welcome and loved. "Feet" stands for the messengers, who bring the best news ever sent from heaven.
The person is saved, but only like someone who escapes a fire after his work is burned up. Bible teachers describe the loss differently: wasted effort, or a lost reward, but not lost salvation.

idioms.idiom: Get rid of the old leaven

meanings.meaning: Clean out the old sin, like Jews who searched their homes to throw out all yeast before Passover. Paul wants the church to live as pure as it already is in Christ.

idioms.idiom: drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons

meanings.meaning: Drinking the Lord's cup means sharing in the Lord's Supper, and drinking the cup of demons means joining idol feasts. You can't have a close relationship with both.
It means they died. The Bible often calls death "sleep," and some at Corinth died after treating the Lord's Supper wrongly, though their souls may still be saved.
Crazy or mad. Visitors who heard everyone speaking in languages they couldn't understand might think the church was a crowd of people acting wildly.
To have died while trusting in Christ. Death is called sleep as a gentle picture, and because the sleeper will wake up again when the dead are raised.
People who have died. The Bible calls death "sleep," especially for believers who died before Christ came back to life, or before He returns.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean Paul faced cruel, beast-like people in Ephesus who threatened his life, or it may mean a real fight with animals.
Not everyone will die. "Sleep" is a gentle word for dying, and Paul says some people will still be alive at the day of judgment, but their bodies will be changed.
Bible teachers aren't sure. It may mean saying yes and no about the same thing, changing plans like worldly people, or insisting on sticking to a decision no matter what.
God has marked us as His own. A seal showed that something belonged to someone, and God's gift of His Spirit is the sign that He will keep His promises.
Nothing blocks believers from seeing the Lord's glory. Moses wore a veil on his face, and others have a veil on their hearts, but for believers it is gone.

idioms.idiom: the earthly tent we live in

meanings.meaning: The "earthly tent" is our body, where the soul lives for a short time. Like a tent, it can be taken down, which happens at death.
"Out of our mind" means seeming not in one's right mind. Some thought Paul was, but he says if so, it is for God; if he is humble and calm, it is for them.

Don't join closely with unbelievers. Bible teachers differ on the picture: mismatched animals at one plow, which includes marriage, or soldiers leaving their ranks, where marriage is only an application.
Paul says he sounds crazy, like someone who has lost his good sense, because he is bragging about himself. He then says he has worked and suffered for Christ even more than his rivals.
Giving the right hand was a sign of trust, friendship, and partnership. The church leaders welcomed Paul and Barnabas as fellow workers who preached the same gospel as they did.

idioms.idiom: you have fallen away from grace

meanings.meaning: Trying to earn God's approval by obeying the law cuts a person off from Christ and His free kindness. Teachers differ on whether they lost grace they had or only claimed it.

idioms.idiom: seated Him at His right hand

meanings.meaning: God gave Jesus the highest place of honor, trust, and power next to Himself. From there Jesus rules over everything and cares for His people, the church.
To make the best use of every chance to do good, like buying up something valuable. Be wise around people outside the church so you help them and don't turn them away.

idioms.idiom: poured out like a drink offering

meanings.meaning: Paul pictures his life, maybe his blood if he is killed, as wine poured on an offering. The offering is the Philippians themselves or their faith, and Paul is glad to give himself for them.
Paul calls false teachers "dogs," a rude name for dirty, snarling troublemakers. Jews used it for Gentiles, but Paul turns it around and warns about these teachers.

idioms.idiom: seated at the right hand of God

meanings.meaning: Christ has the highest place of honor beside God in heaven. He has gone ahead to prepare heavenly happiness for His people.
"Put to death" is not about killing anyone. It means to take away the power of sinful desires by not feeding them or giving in, and letting careful thinking guide you.
Speech that is kind and wise, like salt that keeps food from spoiling and gives it flavor. It keeps talk from being rotten or boring.

idioms.idiom: those who have fallen asleep in Him

meanings.meaning: It means believers who have died. The Bible calls death "sleep" to make it gentler, because believers will be raised again, as Jesus was, and God will bring them with Him.
"Taken out of the way" means the one who now holds back the evil is removed. Then the wicked one, who is now hidden, will be revealed, and everyone will see who he is.
Jesus will defeat the lawless one with just His words. Bible teachers say this means the true message that Jesus saves people, which works over time and is finished when Christ comes back.

idioms.idiom: in season and out of season

meanings.meaning: It means at all times, whether things are going well or badly. Keep telling God's message whenever there is a chance, and even try to make a chance when there seems to be none.
Eager to hear only what feels good. People with itching ears get tired of true teaching and gather many teachers who please them and don't scold them for their wrong wants.

idioms.idiom: being poured out like a drink offering

meanings.meaning: Paul says his life is being poured out like wine offered to God. He knows he will soon die for Christ, and he sees his blood as that offering, which God accepts.
